issues.display_title: Issue #168: Project visibility: is_public column, PATCH key, and the three public read gates
issues.main_description_html:
Backend counterpart to GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#933 (design issue: gothru-3d-floormap#932).

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer
Files: src/models/models.go · src/action/v1/project/update.go · src/action/v1/project/shared.go · src/action/v1/floorplan/live.go · src/action/v1/floorplan/get.go · src/action/v1/files/live_get.go · migrations/

Why now

FE #933 asks for a Public/Private toggle bound to the project update API, and an "This project is private" state for a guest who opens a private project's share link. Neither is possible today: project visibility does not exist at any layer.

  • models.Project (src/models/models.go:55-79) has no is_public / visibility column.
  • newProjectResponse (src/action/v1/project/shared.go:34-52) serializes 15 fields, none of them visibility.
  • PATCH /v1/projects/:id (src/action/v1/project/update.go:47-100) whitelists keys one by one and silently drops anything unknown — a frontend-only visibility PATCH would return 200 and persist nothing.
  • Repo-wide grep for is_public|isPublic|is_private|visibility over *.go/*.sql/*.json returns one prose comment (src/action/v1/project/recent.go:26) and nothing else. docs/swagger.json and docs/postman_collection.json: zero hits.

There are also three route-public read paths, not one. A gate added only to Live leaves a private project fully readable:

Route Handler Current gate
GET /v1/live/:key floorplan/live.go:26 project_key = ? AND status = 'published'
GET /v1/live/:key/file?name= files/live_get.go:47 project_key = ? AND status = 'published'
GET /v1/floorplan/:id floorplan/get.go:34-58 published → anyone; otherwise optional-auth member check

routes/v1/floorplan.go:15-20 registers all three with no auth middleware. /v1/floorplan/:id in particular serves any published project to a fully anonymous caller by UUID — that is the frontend's /preview/{uuid} surface.

Change

1. Column. IsPublic bool on models.Project, gorm:"not null;default:true" json:"is_public", placed beside IsComplete.

Default true on purpose: every existing project stays exactly as reachable as it is today, so this ships with no behaviour change until someone flips a toggle. config/database.go:112 runs AutoMigrate, and migrations/202607200001_add_is_complete_to_projects.sql is the hand-written-SQL convention to mirror:

-- +migrate Up
ALTER TABLE public.projects ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS is_public BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE;

2. PATCH key. Accept isPublic in the update.go whitelist, same shape as isComplete:

if isPublic, ok := updates["isPublic"].(bool); ok {
    dbUpdates["is_public"] = isPublic
}

Note this is untouched by the status guard at update.go:59 — that condition is scoped to the status key alone. Visibility and publish state are two independent axes: /publish and /unpublish keep owning status, PATCH owns is_public. Write access is already gated by the CanWrite check at the top of the handler.

3. Response. IsPublic bool \json:"is_public"`onprojectResponse, set from project.IsPublicinnewProjectResponse`, so get/list/recent/update all carry it.

4. Gates.

  • floorplan/live.go — look the project up by key + published as today; if the row is found and !project.IsPublic, answer 403 {"error": "project is private"}. This is the one endpoint that must be distinguishable, because FE #933 has to render "This project is private" rather than the generic not-available string. Everything else — unknown key, malformed key, unpublished — keeps its identical 404.
  • files/live_get.go — add AND is_public = ? to the existing lookup. No new branch and no new status: a private project's share-card image and floor plans go back to looking exactly like every other miss. The frontend proxies (/api/live/[key]/file, /image) mirror upstream status verbatim, so they need no change.
  • floorplan/get.go — a private project requires membership even when published. Widen the existing condition to if project.Status != "published" || !project.IsPublic { so the optional-auth + FetchRoleForProject block runs for it, and a non-member still gets the same 404. Owners and collaborators keep full access to their own private project's preview and editor.

Deliberate trade-off

The 403 on GET /v1/live/:key tells the caller that this share key exists and is private, where today a private project would be indistinguishable from a missing one. That is inherent to the acceptance criterion — you cannot say "this project is private" without admitting it exists. It is scoped to the one endpoint the share link points at; the file endpoint and the UUID endpoint stay silent.

Acceptance Criteria

  • is_public column exists, defaults to TRUE, and every pre-existing project reads back is_public: true
  • PATCH /v1/projects/{id} with {"isPublic": false} persists, and the same call with {"isPublic": true} flips it back
  • PATCH with isPublic does not change status, and /publish + /unpublish still work on a private project — the two axes are independent
  • is_public is present in the response of get, list, recent and update
  • GET /v1/live/{key} on a published private project → 403 with {"error": "project is private"}; on a published public project → unchanged 200; unknown/unpublished key → unchanged 404
  • GET /v1/live/{key}/file?name= on a published private project → 404, identical to every other miss
  • GET /v1/floorplan/{id} on a published private project → 404 for an anonymous caller, 200 for the owner and for a collaborator
  • Route tests covering the three gates, public and private, anonymous and member
  • go build ./... and go test ./... green

RESULT

PR #169 → development (4a0ea05), release PR #170 → main (2c86560). Work commit 21ca403. 8 files, +216 / −6.

Shipped — Project.IsPublic with gorm:"not null;default:true", so every project that predates the column stays exactly as reachable as it was. isPublic added to the PATCH /v1/projects/:id whitelist beside isComplete; it is untouched by the status guard at update.go:59, which is scoped to that one key. is_public serialized on projectResponse, so get/list/recent/update all carry it.

The three gates — /v1/live/:key answers 403 {"error":"project is private"}, the only endpoint that distinguishes private from missing, because the frontend has to say so. /v1/live/:key/file gained an is_public predicate and rejoins the shared 404, byte-identical to every other miss. /v1/floorplan/:id widened its condition to status != "published" || !IsPublic, so a private project falls back to the optional-auth member check — owner, editor and viewer keep it, a guest gets the same 404 a draft has always returned.

Migration — migrations/202609070001_add_is_public_to_projects.sql. Applied to the database ahead of the release, deliberately: without the column, SELECT * leaves IsPublic false for every row, so /v1/live/:key would have answered 403 to everyone and live_get.go would have thrown a SQL error. Verified after applying: 515 projects, all is_public = true.

Verified — src/routes/v1/project_visibility_test.go, 6 cases. Red-first: with src/action/ stashed, 4 of the 6 fail; restored, go build ./... and go test ./... green. Post-deploy: GET /v1/live/9zg5XR6J → 200 public, 403 private, back to 200 — exercised end to end through the UI while filming the demo.

Noticed, not in scope — schema_migrations does not carry 202608200001_add_event_records_to_projects even though its column exists, so this database's migration history is not purely runner-applied. Worth a look before the next migration assumes the table is authoritative.
